events.text: The fog on the mountain road smells of rice wine and woodsmoke. You walk into it a cultivator and walk out of it on a muddy river bank at dawn, in a patched coat, with calloused hands that are not quite yours. A heron lifts off the water. Somewhere a rooster is crowing. Your qi is gone, as if it had never been.

choices.text: Breathe the morning in

effects.log: You breathe it in. It smells of mud and bread. It is the best thing you have smelled in years.

choices.text: Try to remember who you are

effects.log: You remember: a name, a realm, a road. It is like remembering a dream. You hold on to it anyway.

choices.text: Look for the road you came by

effects.log: There is no road. There is a town on the river, and smoke from its chimneys.

events.text: Deep in the Secret Realm a door of painted silk opens onto a river town in spring. You step through to look, and the door is gone, and so is the realm, and so, you find, is every year of your cultivation. You are standing in a market with a basket on your arm, and someone is asking you the price of eggs.

choices.text: Tell them the price

effects.log: You tell them a price, and they haggle, and you laugh. It is all so ordinary that it hurts.

choices.text: Tell them you are not who they think

effects.log: They look at you oddly and go to the next stall. You are not sure, now, who you are either.

choices.text: Ask the name of the town

effects.log: "Willow Ford," they say, as if you had asked the name of the sky.

events.text: The voice in your heart is kind tonight. "Rest," it says. "Only one life. An ordinary one. I will keep watch." You close your eyes for a moment, and open them on a low ceiling of smoked beams, a straw mat, and the sound of a river. Your hands are a stranger's. Your heart is very quiet.

choices.text: Accept the rest

effects.log: You accept it. The voice does not speak again. Perhaps it is resting too.

choices.text: Distrust the gift

effects.log: Gifts from that voice are never free. You remember that, and keep remembering it.

choices.text: Get up and open the door

effects.log: Outside is a river town in the early light, and the whole of a life.

events.text: In Willow Ford everybody works, and nobody asks where you came from: the river brings people, the river takes people. An old potter needs hands at the wheel. Granny Mak of the ferry steps needs someone to pole the ferry now that her knees are gone. The noodle stall by the bridge needs someone who can stand the steam.

choices.text: Learn the potter's wheel

effects.log: Your first pot collapses. Your tenth stands. By autumn the old potter lets you fire your own.

choices.text: Take the ferry pole

effects.log: Granny Mak watches you push off and shouts at you the whole way across. On the far bank she gives you a rice cake.

choices.text: Stand in the noodle steam

effects.log: The steam takes your eyebrows in the first week. By the second, people are coming back for your broth.

events.text: Years at the wheel. You learn that clay remembers every mistake and forgives most of them in the kiln. Your bowls go up and down the river on every boat. A child from the next street watches you work every afternoon, chin on hands, saying nothing.

choices.text: Let the child try the wheel

effects.log: The child's first bowl is a lump. You fire it anyway, and it sits on the child's family table for years.

choices.text: Work faster, and think of other things

effects.log: Your bowls are perfect, and the afternoons go by, and you think of a sword you used to hold.

events.text: Years on the ferry. You learn every eddy of the river, every passenger's trouble, every way the light falls on the water at evening. Granny Mak sits on the steps and calls out the price for you, and calls you hopeless, and is proud of you, and everyone knows it.

choices.text: Carry Granny Mak home when the cold comes

effects.log: She complains the whole way. That winter she teaches you the ferry songs, all of them.

choices.text: Count the crossings, and wait for something

effects.log: You count the crossings. You are waiting for something. You cannot remember what.

events.text: Years at the noodle stall by the bridge. You learn that a good broth takes all night and is gone by noon, and that people tell the cook things they tell nobody else. You know every debt, every courtship and every grief in Willow Ford, and you keep them all in the broth.

choices.text: Feed the ones who cannot pay

effects.log: You keep a second pot at the back for the ones who cannot pay. Nobody mentions it. Everybody knows.

choices.text: Keep the stall and nothing else

effects.log: You keep the stall, and your counsel, and yourself apart. The broth is very good.

events.text: Haneul from the dyer's house on the far bank has been finding reasons to come by for a year. Nobody in Willow Ford is surprised when the matchmaker comes too, with a red cloth and a pot of plum wine, and sits down on your step to wait for an answer.

choices.text: Say yes

effects.log: You say yes. The wedding is small and loud and the whole street comes. Haneul's hands are blue with dye for the ceremony.

choices.text: Thank them, and stay alone

effects.log: You thank the matchmaker and send the wine back. Haneul waves to you from the far bank for the rest of the year, kindly.

events.text: The matchmaker comes with a red cloth and a pot of plum wine, and behind her, shy, comes Haneul from the dyer's house. You look up, and your breath stops. The face is {mdr_kin}'s. Not like it: exactly it. Even the dream, it seems, knows who you would choose.

choices.text: Say yes, with your whole heart

effects.log: You say yes before the matchmaker has finished. Haneul laughs, {mdr_kin}'s laugh. You will not think about what that means. Not yet.

choices.text: Say no, because it is not really them

effects.log: You say no. It is the hardest word you have ever said in any life. Haneul goes home across the river.

events.text: A child comes, in the spring floods, in the middle of the night, red and furious and perfect. You call the child Bori, after the barley that was coming up. Haneul laughs and says that is a name for a field, and calls the child Bori anyway.

choices.text: Walk the floor all night with Bori

effects.log: You walk the floor until dawn, every night for a season. You have never been so tired, or so sure of anything.

choices.text: Leave the nights to Haneul

effects.log: Haneul walks the floor, and you work. It is a fair division, everyone says. You are not sure.

events.text: A child of the river streets named Jun turns up at your door one winter, too thin, too proud to ask. You give the apprentice a bowl and a corner to sleep in. It is supposed to be for the winter. It is for years.

choices.text: Teach Jun everything you know

effects.log: You teach Jun the work, then the trade, then the town. By the end Jun does it better than you.

choices.text: Teach Jun only the work

effects.log: You teach Jun the work. Jun learns it, and learns not to ask for more.

events.text: The kiln cracks in the coldest week of the year, with a whole season's work inside it. You could feel the crack coming, the way you used to feel a blade. For a moment, deep in your chest, something stirs that is not a potter's: a breath of qi, from very far away.

choices.text: Rebuild the kiln brick by brick, like anyone

effects.log: It takes all winter and every friend you have. The first firing in spring is the best of your life.

choices.text: Reach for that far-off qi

effects.log: The qi answers, a little. The kiln seals itself in a breath. The whole dream shudders, and you are afraid, and do not know why.

events.text: The river floods in the year of the long rains, and the ferry is the only way across for a week. You pole until your hands bleed and your shoulders burn, and the water keeps rising. In the worst of it, something in your chest remembers how to make the body stronger.

choices.text: Keep poling, as a ferryman would

effects.log: You keep poling. Every family gets across. Afterwards Granny Mak cries, which nobody has ever seen.

choices.text: Let the old strength into your arms

effects.log: The strength comes. The ferry flies. Willow Ford watches you strangely afterwards, and the sky above it flickers.

events.text: A lean winter: no rice on the boats, no meat in the market, and a line at your stall that goes back over the bridge. You know a way, from somewhere, to make a pot of broth go much further than it should. It is not a cook's way.

choices.text: Water the broth, and share it out

effects.log: The broth is thin, and there is some for everyone, and nobody in Willow Ford starves that winter.

choices.text: Use the way that is not a cook's

effects.log: The pot does not empty. The line goes home full. That night the stars over the town are in the wrong places.

events.text: You grow old in Willow Ford. Your knees go the way Granny Mak's did. Bori is grown, and has children of their own, and the youngest of them, Little Sol, sits on your lap in the evenings and asks for stories. You find you only know ordinary ones, and that they are enough.

choices.text: Tell Little Sol a story about a river

effects.log: You tell it, and Little Sol falls asleep before the end, and Haneul, grey now too, finishes it for you.

choices.text: Tell Little Sol a story about a sword

effects.log: You tell a story about a sword that could cut the sky. Little Sol loves it. You are not sure where it came from.

events.text: You grow old in Willow Ford. Jun runs the business now, and has an apprentice too, and they both bring you your tea in the mornings and argue about how it should be made. Your hands shake. The river is the same as ever.

choices.text: Sit with them while they argue

effects.log: You sit with them. The argument is the best part of the morning. You tell them so, and they both stop, embarrassed.

choices.text: Sit by the river alone

effects.log: You sit by the river. You keep thinking you are waiting for someone to come along the bank. Nobody does.

events.text: One evening, very old, on the step of the house in Willow Ford, you hear someone call a name. It is not the name anyone here calls you. It is your real one, from very far away, from a mountain road in the fog, and you know that if you answer, all of this will end. The river is the same as ever. Supper is nearly ready.

choices.text: Answer, and wake

effects.log: You answer. Willow Ford goes thin, like paper held up to a lamp.

choices.text: Do not answer: stay

effects.log: You do not answer. The voice calls once more, fainter.

choices.text: Wait a little, then answer

effects.log: You wait until the river turns gold, and then you answer.

events.text: One evening, very old, on the step of the house in Willow Ford, with the sound of your people inside, you hear someone call a name: your real one, from a mountain road in the fog. You know what it means. You have lived this life so fully that leaving it will feel like dying, and staying will be dying, somewhere else.

choices.text: Answer, and take them with you in your heart

effects.log: You go inside first and look at each of them, for as long as you can. Then you answer.

choices.text: Do not answer: stay with them

effects.log: You do not answer. Inside, someone is laughing. The voice calls once more, fainter.

choices.text: Answer at once, before you cannot

effects.log: You answer at once, while you still can. Willow Ford goes thin, like paper held up to a lamp.

events.text: If you stay, the voice will stop calling. In Willow Ford you will finish this life, and then nothing. Far away, on a mountain road, your real body will sit in the fog, smiling, until it withers. Everything you were before the fog will end there, and nobody will know why. This is the end of the life you came from. Are you sure?

choices.text: Stay for good

effects.log: You stay.

choices.text: Wake after all

effects.log: Not yet, you think. Not like this. You answer the voice.

events.text: Dawn on the mountain road. Dew on your sleeves. Your qi is back, roaring like a river after rain, and it feels very loud. One night has passed. Your hands still remember the work of a whole life, and the weight of a sleeping child, and you do not think they will ever forget.

choices.text: Sit in the road and weep a little

effects.log: You weep for Willow Ford. Then you get up. Grief, it turns out, is also an insight.

choices.text: Bow toward a river you cannot see

effects.log: You bow toward a town that is not there. It feels like the truest thing you have done in years.

events.text: Dawn on the mountain road. Your qi is back, and your name, and the long road you were walking. The dream is already going, the way dreams go: a river, a town, an ordinary life. You held a little of yourself back the whole time. You are not sure, now, whether that was wise.

choices.text: Walk on

effects.log: You walk on. The ordinary world looks a little different. Heavier. Kinder.

choices.text: Try to hold on to what is left

effects.log: You hold on to a smell of broth, a song, a step by a river. It is enough to be going on with.

events.text: You walk past a potter's shop and stop dead. The smell of the kiln. You have never touched clay in your life, and your hands know exactly how it would feel. You stand there until the potter asks if you are all right.

choices.text: Ask if you may try the wheel

effects.log: Your first bowl stands. The potter stares at it, and then at you.

choices.text: Say you are fine, and walk on

effects.log: You walk on. Your hands keep the feeling all day.

events.text: An old storyteller tells of a cultivator who fell asleep in a fog on a mountain road and never woke, and was found years later, smiling. "They say," the storyteller adds, "there is a river town somewhere that remembers them fondly." Your eyes sting, and you cannot think why.

choices.text: Ask the name of the town

effects.log: "Willow Ford," the storyteller says. "Though nobody has ever found it."

choices.text: Raise your tea to the one who stayed

effects.log: You raise your cup of tea to them. It feels like toasting an old friend.
